body.p: In the Office Action, claims 1, 2, 15, 19 and 20 were objected to because of informalities. Claims 1, 2, 15, 19 and 20 have been amended as suggested by the Examiner, and withdrawal of the objection to the claims is respectfully requested.

Claims 1-9, 12-14 and 16-17 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as being indefinite. Claim 1 has been amended as suggested by the Examiner, and is clear for the purposes of Section 112. Withdrawal of the Section 112 rejection is respectfully requested.

Additionally, claims 1-6, 12, 14-18 and 20 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Seeley et al. (US 6,561,600) in view of Shah (US 9,360,895). Claims 7-9 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Seeley in view of Chavarria et al. (US 11,365,006). Finally, claim 19 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Seeley in view of Shah and Chavarria, and further in view of Tuccinardi et al. (US 7,040,697). Applicant respectfully traverses the foregoing and requests reconsideration.

Notwithstanding the foregoing traversal, solely in an effort to expedite prosecution, Applicant had amended claims 1, 15, and 20 to recite "wherein each of the at least two first fastening elements is oriented in the same direction along the fastening direction, and each of the at least two second fastening elements is oriented in the same direction along the fastening direction." This amendment is supported and adds no new matter. See Published Application FIG. 2; 0021 and 0057. As shown in Applicant's FIG. 2, each of the fastening elements 24 is oriented in the same direction, and each of the fastening elements 26 is oriented in the same direction.
The Examiner acknowledges that Seeley fails to disclose wherein each of the at least two first fastening elements are displaced from one another along the fastening direction,

and wherein each of the at least two second fastening elements are displaced from one another along the fastening direction. See Office Action page 6. Shah fails to resolve the deficiencies of Seeley.

Shah discloses an assembly 10 for mounting a display device 12 to the back of a seat 14 of the vehicle. The assembly 10 also includes a mounting plate 16 which includes opposite edges 25 and 27 and at least one locking mechanism 28, "mounted proximate one of the edges 25 or 27 of the mounting plate 16. Preferably, there is another locking mechanism 28 proximate the other edge 25 or 27 of the mounting plate 16." See Shah Col. 5, 11. 40-45. Regarding the locking mechanism 28, Shah states:

Each locking mechanism 28 includes a jaw 30 extending over the front surface 18 of the mounting plate 16. In particular, the jaw 30 projects over its respective edge 25 or 27 of the mounting plate 16. Thereafter, a lip 32 projects parallel to the front surface 18 of the mounting plate 16 towards the
lateral axis of the mounting plate 16.

As shown in FIG. 2, Shah also discloses a bracket structure 52 which "includes upper and lower edges 54 and 56. One edge 54 of the bracket structure 52 is engaged by one of the locking mechanisms 28 and the other edge 56 is engaged by the other locking mechanism 28." Shah Col. 6, 11. 30-36. Therefore, as shown in FIGs. 1, 3, and 4A, Shah discloses locking elements 28, which are oriented toward one another. In other words, Shah fails to disclose or suggest first and second fastening elements which are oriented in the same direction along the fastening direction. Additionally, any modification of Shah according to claims 1, 15, and 20 would render Shah inoperative.

Accordingly, the cited references fail to disclose or suggest all of the features of claims 1, 15, and 20. Thus, claims 1, 15, and 20 should be allowable over the cited art. Those claims that depend therefrom should be allowable as well at least by virtue of their claim dependency.

Applicant therefore respectfully submits that all of the claims of the application should be found to be allowable and thus requests that the Examiner indicate all of the claims as allowed and pass the application to allowance.

Furthermore, the fact that Applicant has only addressed certain rej ections should not be considered to be acquiescence to the rejections. Rather, Applicant has presented the argument herein in an effort to expedite prosecution. Applicant reserves any and all rights to address any rejection made but not specifically addressed herein.
The Commissioner is hereby authorized to charge any additional fees which may be required to this application under 37 C.F.R. § § 1.16-1.17, or credit any overpayment, to Deposit Account No. 07-2069.
Should the Examiner discover there are remaining issues which may be resolved by a telephone interview, the Examiner is invited to contact the undersigned attorney at (312) 600-6841.
